project.name: E-Commerce Platform
project.summary: Online marketplace for customers to browse, purchase, and track orders, with seller product management and admin oversight.

functional_requirements: Customers can browse the product catalogue
Customers can add products to a shopping cart
Customers can checkout and pay online
Sellers can list products and manage inventory
Administrators can approve sellers and process refund requests
non_functional_requirements: The system must enforce secure authentication and data encryption
The platform must scale to support high concurrent user traffic
Response time for user actions should be under 2 seconds

actors.name: Customer
actors.description: Browses products, adds items to cart, makes purchases, and tracks orders

actors.name: Seller
actors.description: Lists products, updates inventory, and fulfills orders after approval

actors.name: Administrator
actors.description: Approves seller registrations, manages refunds, and oversees platform governance

use_cases.name: Browse Catalogue
use_cases.description: Customer searches and views product listings

use_cases.name: Add to Cart
use_cases.description: Customer selects products and adds them to a shopping cart

use_cases.name: Checkout and Pay
use_cases.description: Customer completes payment using an online payment gateway

use_cases.name: List and Manage Products
use_cases.description: Seller creates product entries and updates stock levels

use_cases.name: Approve Seller and Process Refund
use_cases.description: Administrator reviews seller applications and handles customer refund requests

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Customers can browse the product catalogue
criteria: Search results return relevant products within 1 second
Product details page displays price, images, and description

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Customers can add products to a shopping cart
criteria: Item appears in cart immediately after selection
Cart persists across user sessions

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Customers can checkout and pay online
criteria: Payment succeeds with supported gateways and returns confirmation
Order summary email is sent within 5 minutes of purchase

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Sellers can list products and manage inventory
criteria: Seller can create, edit, and delete product listings
Inventory count updates in real time after sales

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Administrators can approve sellers and process refund requests
criteria: Seller approval workflow notifies seller within 24 hours
Refunds are processed and reflected in payment system within 48 hours

user_stories.story: As a customer, I want to browse the product catalogue, so that I can find items to purchase.
acceptance_criteria: The catalogue displays product name, image, price, and stock status.
Customers can filter and search products by category, name, or price.

user_stories.story: As a customer, I want to add products to a shopping cart, so that I can purchase multiple items in one order.
acceptance_criteria: Items can be added, updated quantity, and removed from the cart.
Cart persists across user sessions until checkout or explicit clearing.

user_stories.story: As a customer, I want to pay online securely, so that my transaction is safe and completed quickly.
acceptance_criteria: Payment gateway supports credit/debit cards and tokenized payment methods.
Sensitive data is encrypted in transit and not stored on the platform.

user_stories.story: As a seller, I want to list new products after approval, so that I can start selling them.
acceptance_criteria: Approved sellers can create product entries with title, description, price, and inventory.
New listings become visible to customers only after successful submission.

user_stories.story: As an administrator, I want to approve seller accounts, so that only vetted sellers can list products.
acceptance_criteria: Admin can view pending seller applications and approve or reject them.
Rejected sellers receive a notification with the reason for denial.

user_stories.story: As an administrator, I want to handle refund requests, so that customers receive timely reimbursements.
acceptance_criteria: Admin can view, approve, or deny refund requests with status updates.
Customers are notified of the refund decision and amount refunded.

UML Generator.use_case:
flowchart LR
    Customer -->|Browse| BrowseCatalog
    Customer -->|Add to Cart| AddToCart
    Customer -->|Pay| OnlinePayment
    Customer -->|Track| TrackOrder
    Seller -->|List Products| ListProduct
    Seller -->|Manage Inventory| ManageInventory
    Admin -->|Approve Sellers| ApproveSeller
    Admin -->|Handle Refunds| HandleRefund
UML Generator.sequence:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Customer
    participant UI as WebApp
    participant PS as ProductService
    participant CS as CartService
    participant PG as PaymentGateway
    participant OS as OrderService
    participant S as Seller
    C->>UI: BrowseCatalog
    UI->>PS: GetProducts
    PS-->>UI: ProductList
    C->>UI: AddToCart(productId)
    UI->>CS: AddItem(productId)
    CS-->>UI: UpdatedCart
    C->>UI: Checkout
    UI->>PG: ProcessPayment(details)
    PG-->>UI: PaymentSuccess
    UI->>OS: CreateOrder(cart)
    OS-->>UI: OrderConfirmed
    OS->>S: NotifyOrder(orderId)
    UI-->>C: OrderConfirmed

relationships.description: A seller (user) can list many products
A customer can place many orders
A product can appear in many order items

Database Designer.sql:
CREATE TABLE Users (
    user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name TEXT,
    email TEXT,
    password_hash TEXT,
    is_seller BOOLEAN,
    is_admin BOOLEAN
);

CREATE TABLE Products (
    product_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    seller_id INTEGER,
    name TEXT,
    description TEXT,
    price REAL,
    stock INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (seller_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Orders (
    order_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    user_id INTEGER,
    order_date DATETIME,
    total_amount REAL,
    status TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE OrderItems (
    item_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    order_id INTEGER,
    product_id INTEGER,
    quantity INTEGER,
    unit_price REAL,
    FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES Orders(order_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES Products(product_id)
);

Project Structure.architecture: Micro‑service style monolith: a FastAPI backend exposing REST/GraphQL endpoints, a React/Vite SPA, PostgreSQL for relational data, Redis for session cache and async task queue (Celery). Docker composes services, Nginx terminates TLS and load‑balances. CI/CD pipelines enforce testing and container deployment.
Project Structure.architecture_diagram:
flowchart TD
    subgraph Client
        A[React SPA] --> B[API Gateway (Nginx)]
    end
    subgraph Server
        B --> C[FastAPI Service]
        C --> D[PostgreSQL]
        C --> E[Redis]
        C --> F[Celery Workers]
    end
    C --> G[Stripe Payment API]
    F --> D
    style A fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style C fill:#bbf,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px

Documentation.readme: E‑Commerce Platform: customers browse catalog, add to cart, checkout, track orders. Sellers list products, manage inventory after admin approval. Admins approve sellers, handle refunds. Built with Node.js, Express, React, PostgreSQL, Redis, Stripe, JWT. Secure, scalable, fast.
Documentation.api_documentation: POST /api/auth/login – JWT auth. GET /api/products – list with filters. GET /api/products/:id – details. POST /api/cart – add item. GET /api/cart – view cart. POST /api/checkout – Stripe payment. GET /api/orders – user orders. POST /api/sellers – register (admin approve). PUT /api/sellers/:id/inventory – update stock. POST /api/admin/refunds – process refund.
Documentation.installation: Clone repo, run `npm install` in server and client folders. Set env vars: DB_URL, REDIS_URL, JWT_SECRET, STRIPE_KEY. Run `npm run db:migrate`. Start with `npm start` (server) and `npm run dev` (client).
Documentation.deployment: Containerize with Docker. Use Docker Compose for app, db, redis. Deploy to Kubernetes or managed service. Configure HTTPS via Let’s Encrypt. Enable autoscaling and health checks. Use CI/CD pipeline for automated builds.
Documentation.sprint_plan: Sprint 1: Core catalog, product API, DB schema. Sprint 2: Cart & checkout integration with Stripe. Sprint 3: Seller onboarding, inventory management, admin approval flow. Sprint 4: Order tracking, refund API, admin dashboard. Sprint 5: Security hardening, load testing, CI/CD setup.
Documentation.architecture: Frontend React SPA communicates with Node/Express REST API. PostgreSQL stores users, products, orders; Redis caches catalog and sessions. Stripe handles payments. JWT secures endpoints. Kubernetes orchestrates services; Ingress provides TLS. Horizontal pods ensure scalability.
